summary: Order-submit failures (~31% error rate, 504s) are caused by the EXTERNAL exchange partner API (api.exchange-partner.example) degrading: exchange-gateway logs upstream connect timeouts after 5000ms and 503 Service Unavailable from the partner starting 11:01:25, and upstream_latency jumped from ~118ms to ~8500ms. order-service simply propagates those 504/503s on placeOrder. Root cause category is dependency_failure originating at the external exchange-api. The order-service v2.15.2 release (idempotency keys, deployed 10:48) is coincidental timing: its rollback at 11:16 did NOT restore service (error rate still ~31% through 12:45), order-service CPU/memory/restarts are normal, and no idempotency-related errors appear in any logs. The incident was still ongoing at 12:58 (latest data). Note: the reported "rolling back order-service" action will not fix this; a secondary exchange route / partner failover is needed.

ranked_hypotheses.title: External exchange partner API degrading (connect timeouts / 503)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The external exchange provider api.exchange-partner.example began timing out connections (5s) and returning 503 Service Unavailable around 11:01. exchange-gateway's calls to it fail, producing 504s that order-service surfaces on placeOrder (~31% error rate). exchange-gateway and order-service are victims, not causes.

causal_chain.claim: exchange-api (external partner) starts refusing/timing out connections
exchange-gateway upstream_latency rises to ~8.5s and upstream_error_rate to ~42-46%
exchange-gateway returns 504/503 to order-service on placeOrder
order-service propagates 504s -> ~31% error rate and p99 ~5.3s

assumptions: exchange-api has no telemetry (vendor), so the fault can only be inferred from gateway-side symptoms
the external partner's degradation is the true origin rather than a network path shared only by our gateway

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.15.2 release introduced the fault
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The idempotency-keys release v2.15.2 broke order submit, causing ~31% failures.

causal_chain.claim: rollback should restore service but did not

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Rolling back v2.15.2 at 11:16 did not restore service (error rate stayed ~31% through 12:45). All errors are exchange-gateway 504s, unrelated to idempotency; no 'idempot' log lines appear; order-service CPU/memory/restarts are normal.

ranked_hypotheses.title: exchange-gateway resource exhaustion / saturation
ranked_hypotheses.statement: exchange-gateway ran out of CPU/connections and timed out its upstream calls.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: exchange-gateway cpu_pct flat ~30% and request_rate flat ~273 req/s; the timeouts are on the outbound call to the external partner, not local resource pressure.

ranked_hypotheses.title: pricing-engine cache TTL config change caused failures
ranked_hypotheses.statement: cfg-2290 (cache.ttl_seconds 5->4) degraded pricing-engine and cascaded to order-service.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: pricing-engine error_rate stayed ~0.2% and latency_p99 ~60ms throughout, and order-service errors are all exchange-gateway 504s, not pricing-engine calls.

facts.statement: order-service error_rate rose from ~0.2% to ~31% at the 11:00 bucket and remained ~31% through 12:45.
order-service error logs are exclusively 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)' (174 matches).
exchange-gateway logged upstream connect timeouts after 5000ms to host=api.exchange-partner.example and 503 Service Unavailable from exchange-api, beginning 11:01:25.
exchange-gateway upstream_latency_ms rose from ~118ms to ~8500-9300ms at the 11:00 bucket and stayed elevated through 12:45.
order-service latency_p99_ms rose from ~150ms to ~5300ms coincident with the failures.
exchange-gateway request_rate, cpu_pct (~30%) and order-service cpu_pct (~40%), memory_pct (~60%) all remained flat, and order-service restarts stayed 0.
order-service v2.15.2 (idempotency keys) was deployed 10:48 and rolled back 11:16, but the error rate stayed ~31% after the rollback.
No logs matching 'idempot' exist in order-service during 10:40-11:20, and no exchange-gateway deployments occurred in the window.
Historical incident HIST-103 was an external exchange partner API outage producing 504s on order submit via exchange-gateway (category dependency_failure).
The exchange partner failures were still occurring at 12:58 (latest data).

assumptions: exchange-api (external partner) has no telemetry available, so its failure is inferred from exchange-gateway observations rather than directly measured.
order-service deploy timing (10:48) is coincidental to the 11:01 exchange-api onset; we cannot fully exclude a shared network-path cause between our gateway and the partner.
Latency/error metric buckets are 15 min, so exact onset is bounded to ~11:00-11:01.

timeline.event: Config change cfg-2290: pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5->4 (no observed impact).
First exchange-gateway upstream connect timeout to api.exchange-partner.example (placeOrder).
First order-service ERROR: exchange-gateway call failed 504 on placeOrder.
exchange-gateway circuit breaker OPEN for exchange-api.
order-service v2.15.2 rolled back - service does NOT recover.
order-service error_rate still ~31%; exchange-gateway upstream_latency still ~9.2s.
exchange-gateway still logging upstream connect timeouts (incident ongoing).

recommended_actions.action: Stop / do not rely on the order-service rollback to fix this - the rollback already occurred (11:16) without recovery; restore v2.15.2 if it is otherwise fine.
recommended_actions.rationale: The error rate stayed ~31% after rollback and the fault is external, so the rollback does not address the cause.

recommended_actions.action: Engage the exchange partner and/or fail over to the secondary exchange route; verify exchange-api health directly with the vendor.
recommended_actions.rationale: All failures trace to api.exchange-partner.example connect timeouts/503s; the fix is on the vendor side or via failover.

recommended_actions.action: Tune exchange-gateway resilience: shorter connect timeout, keep circuit breaker open with graceful degradation, and queue/retry idempotent placeOrder calls for when the partner recovers.
recommended_actions.rationale: 5000ms timeouts propagate as order-submit latency/504s (~5.3s p99); fast-fail would reduce blast radius.

recommended_actions.action: Add partner-side synthetics/alerting on exchange-api upstream_error_rate and latency so vendor degradation is detected before it manifests as order failures.
recommended_actions.rationale: The vendor has no telemetry (exchange-api external, has_telemetry false) and detection lagged the 11:01 onset.

data_gaps: No direct telemetry for exchange-api (external vendor, has_telemetry: false) - vendor-side cause (their outage vs. our network egress path) cannot be distinguished from our data.

order-service log query for 'idempot' returned 0 in 10:40-11:20, but this narrow window does not cover the full deploy duration; idempotency-specific failures can't be fully excluded, though all observed order errors are exchange-gateway 504s.
15-minute metric buckets bound onset precision to roughly 11:00-11:01; exact second of exchange-api degradation unknown.
No packets/network telemetry to confirm whether the failure is the partner's service or connectivity between our egress and the partner.

findings.statement: order-service error_rate jumped from a ~0.2% baseline to 26.73% at the 11:00-11:15 bucket and stayed ~31% (still 30.99 at 12:45).
All 174 order-service ERROR entries in 10:30-12:00 match one pattern: 'exchange-gateway call failed: <n> Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)' (504).

The fault originates at the external exchange provider (exchange-api); exchange-gateway and order-service are downstream victims propagating the partner's timeouts/503s.
